topic: Broader positioning. The same idea applies to calls, quotes and follow-up.

slides.subtitle: (so does the best front office)
slides.scene: A single work truck parked on a residential driveway at night with its lights off. The truck has COMPLETELY BLANK doors and body panels with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind anywhere on the vehicle. No signage anywhere in the scene, including on the house behind. There is NO text, no words, no labels and no captions anywhere in the image. Four thin Scaile blue lines arc out from the truck into the dark, each ending in a small glowing point, and nothing is written beside them.

caption:
The reason this account posts twice a day is not that we are disciplined. It is that posting was turned into something that happens on its own.

Which raises the obvious question about everything else.

The call that came in at nine last night. The quote you sent on Tuesday that nobody chased. The customer from two winters ago who has not heard from you since. The review you never asked for.

Every one of those is the same shape of problem. It is not difficult work. It is work that has to happen at a moment you are physically unable to do it, so it does not happen at all.

Social media is the least important one on that list, and it is the one we automated first because it was easy to show. The others are worth more.

If you want to see what that looks like on your own numbers, book a twenty minute walkthrough at scaileai.com.
